name: Cauliflower
grown_as: Cauliflower, cut for its white curd. William's records list 'All the Year Round' (white), 'Romanesco' (lime-green pointed spirals) and 'Di Sicilia Violetto' (purple). Drawn white, the most typical. ⚠️ CHECK.
habit: An upright plant 45 to 60 cm tall with long leaves held upright round a single domed white curd 15 to 20 cm across at the top of a thick short stem. Left uncut, the curd loosens and grows into a branched flowering stem 1 m or more.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, spiralling on the stem, close together; the inner ones curve up and over the curd
leaf.outline: Long and oblong to elliptic, 40 to 60 cm, more upright, longer and narrower than a cabbage leaf
leaf.base: Narrowing into a short, thick stalk
leaf.margin: Wavy, shallowly scalloped, no sharp teeth
leaf.veins: A thick pale midrib and pale side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless, smooth, with a waxy grey bloom

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, broad and rounded with a long narrow claw, spreading flat
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers, round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright green sepals hugging the petal claws
flower.carried: In long, loose spikes on a tall branched stem; the closed buds stay above the open flowers at the top of each spike

fruit: Long, slender pods 5 to 10 cm, cylindrical with slight bumps over the seeds, ending in a short beak 0.5 to 1 cm, spreading upwards along the stems. Green, drying straw-brown and splitting from the bottom to show a pale papery partition. Seeds round, 2 mm, dark red-brown to grey-black.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, waxy grey-green; the first true leaves oval to round on long stalks, waxy blue-green with wavy edges.
winter: Winter-heading varieties stand through the cold; most are cut by late autumn.

leaf: a long oblong blade with a wavy edge, no sharp teeth
bloom: four pale yellow rounded petals in a cross
narrow upright sepals hugging the claws
closed buds above the open flowers
seed: round dark red-brown to grey-black seed 2 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: an upright plant of long waxy blue-green leaves
crop: a dense domed creamy-white curd with a knobbly surface of tight florets
long upright blue-green leaves around it, the inner ones curving over it
flower: the curd loosened and grown into branching stems
pale yellow four-petalled flowers in loose spikes
seedhead: long slender pods with short beaks along tall stems

look_alikes: Broccoli has a green head of separate tiny flower buds rather than a smooth curd. Romanesco has pointed spiralling cones. All the cabbage-family crops (cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, sprouts, kale) are one species and share the waxy blue-green leaf; they differ in what is eaten. Swede and oilseed rape have bluish clasping stem leaves but their young leaves are hairy. Turnip and pak choi (Brassica rapa) have bright yellow flowers held above their buds.
